grammatik.regel: *can* is a modal verb. It has the same form for every person (he _can_, no -s). The next verb is in the base form: I _can_ *cook*. Question: _Can_ you *cook*? Negative: I _can't_ *cook*.

soGehts: The street party is on Saturday. Who can do what? Who can help?
Cut page 2 in half. Partner A takes the left half, Partner B the right half.
On your own: Put the words in order and write the questions.
In pairs: Ask your partner. Write down the answer (yes / no / a bit).
Tell the class: What can your partner do? How can they help at the party?

hinweise: Can does not change: can I, can you, can she.
The next verb stays in the base form: Can you cook? (not cooks).
Answer: Yes, I can. / No, I can't. / A bit.

zusammen.titel: Together: Who helps at the party?
freiFragen: Who can cook or bake? – … can bake a cake. She/He makes the cake.
Who can make music? Who can take photos?
What can't you do at all? – I can't …

loesungen.antwort: Partner A: Can you cook well? · Can you play the guitar? · Can you bake a cake? · Can you take good photos? · Can you repair bikes?
Partner B: Can you sing well? · Can you drive a car? · Can you paint well? · Can you speak Spanish? · Can you make music?
Report, for example: My partner can cook very well, but she can't play the guitar. At the party she can bake a cake.
